current_fund.raw: US$70M raised toward initial US$100M target (May 2022)

check_size.raw: US$300,000 to US$5 million per company ($250,000 to $5 million per some reports)

strategy.thesis: Canada's first institutional crypto-native venture fund. Backs blockchain infrastructure companies solving interoperability and scalability, plus teams building top-tier applications on those rails. Open-ended structure with quarterly investment opportunities; spans AI, gaming/metaverse, identity, and infrastructure.

summary.en: Toronto-based crypto-native venture fund launched by Round13 Capital in 2022. Branded 'Canada's first institutional crypto-native venture fund,' it raised US$70M (toward an initial US$100M target, ~US$80M total by 2024) led by a major Canadian pension fund. Invests US$300K–$5M into ~20 seed/Series A blockchain and Web3 companies including ChainSafe, Wombo, Improbable Worlds and Trust Machines.

verification_notes: Check-size figures differ slightly across sources (US$300K–$5M per BetaKit launch coverage vs $250K–$5M per 2024 performance coverage); both reported. Dedicated fund site r13daf.com has lapsed (domain now parked/for sale) and round13.com no longer lists a crypto/digital-asset strategy on its homepage, so the fund may be winding down or no longer actively raising — status set to 'active' based on investments recorded through 2024–2025, but this is uncertain.

strategy.thesis: Venture arm of digital-asset infrastructure firm Aquanow. Backs early-stage companies addressing problems across the technology stack for financial-service businesses building in crypto — payments, infrastructure and compliance — that tie into Aquanow's core digital-asset infrastructure business.

people.name: Michael Kwok
people.role: Head of Venture Capital, AQN Digital

summary.en: Venture fund of Aquanow, a Canadian digital-asset infrastructure firm established in 2018 (offices in Toronto and Vancouver). Launched September 2023 and valued at $13.4M CAD (US$10M), the fund writes $100K–$500K checks into early-stage blockchain startups across payments, infrastructure and compliance. By launch it had deployed ~$1M into seven companies including BoomFi and Mash, targeting up to two investments per month.

Fund is structured as the corporate venture arm of an operating crypto-infrastructure company, hence type 'cvc'. Aquanow's main site now emphasizes UAE/Dubai operations, but the venture fund and Canadian roots are well documented.

summary.en: Toronto-based Web3 venture firm focused on the blockchain x AI ('decentralized AI') intersection. In April 2024 it announced a $5M first close on a targeted $10M Blockchain x AI Seed Fund, writing $150K–$250K checks into North American seed-stage companies. Run by managing partners Mike Grantis and Joshua Field, who have made 80+ angel investments since the firm's 2021 inception; portfolio includes Hivello, Koat.ai, Coinweb and Kado.

strategy.thesis: $725M ecosystem fund to drive innovation across the Flow blockchain (created by Dapper Labs). Supports developers building on Flow via investments, FLOW token grants and in-kind support, focused on gaming, infrastructure, decentralized finance, content and creators. Capital is jointly committed alongside external VCs including a16z, Coatue, USV, CoinFund and DCG.

summary.en: Vancouver-based Dapper Labs (creator of Flow, NBA Top Shot and CryptoKitties) launched a $725M Flow Ecosystem Fund in May 2022 — described as the largest joint commitment to any blockchain ecosystem. It funds developers building on Flow through investments, FLOW token grants and in-kind support across gaming, infrastructure, DeFi and creators, with capital committed alongside external VCs such as a16z, Coatue, USV, CoinFund and DCG.

verification_notes: Borderline inclusion: the $725M figure is a joint commitment pooled across many external VCs (a16z, Coatue, USV, etc.), not a single Canadian-managed fund — Dapper Labs' own vehicle is 'Dapper Ventures.' Included because Dapper Labs (Vancouver) is the Canadian operator anchoring the fund. Investment mechanics blend equity, FLOW token grants and in-kind support rather than pure VC checks, so check_size left null. founded_year reflects the fund's 2022 launch, not Dapper Labs' company founding (~2018).
